subject: POC: trial plan & traffic profile — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@acme-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: POC follow-up: trial objectives & traffic intake

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap to make sure we’re aligned before we draft a formal Statement of Work for the trial: 

- Primary objective: validate that Redwood can serve Acme’s product-recommendation API at acceptable latency and cost while preserving data controls (no customer PII leaves Acme environment).
- Duration: 4 weeks of hands-on evaluation (2-week smoke/ramp, 2-week steady-state plus analysis).
- Success criteria (initial): 
  - p50 latency <= 80ms for 8k token window, p95 latency <= 250ms under steady-state load
  - Sustained throughput: 120 requests/sec (RPS) with peak bursts up to 450 RPS for short windows
  - Cost target: estimated <= $X per million tokens (we’ll provide modeling)

Action items I need from your side to finalize the POC plan: 
1) Traffic profile (CSV or short summary) showing typical RPS, peak RPS (burst duration), average & 95th-percentile token lengths per request, concurrency, and time-of-day patterns. Example columns: timestamp, rps, avg_tokens, p95_tokens, concurrent_users.
2) Test endpoints and authentication mechanism we should use for the smoke test (API key, mTLS, or short-lived token).
3) Security/compliance must-haves: do you need Dedicated or Private (VPC) for the trial? Any specific IP allowlists or egress restrictions?
4) Point people: technical owner for the trial (we had Tom on the call), procurement contact for contract/PO.

I attached a one-page draft MOP (acme_poc_mop_v1.pdf) and an example traffic CSV template (traffic_sample_202602.csv) to make the intake easier.

If you can send the traffic profile and confirm owners by Friday (Mar 6), we’ll aim to kick off the week of Mar 9 and deliver the initial smoke results within 3 business days.

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick call if that helps.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: acme_poc_mop_v1.pdf, traffic_sample_202602.csv

Hi Ben —

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers below: 

1) Traffic profile (high level):
   - Typical RPS (global): 45 RPS during peak business hours
   - Steady-state target for POC: 120 RPS (we want to validate beyond current peak)
   - Burst behavior: spikes up to 450 RPS for 3–7 minute windows (promo events)
   - Avg token length per request: 420 tokens; p95 token length: 2,800 tokens (recommendation/rationale text heavy)
   - Expected concurrency: 180 concurrent request streams during peak spikes

2) Authentication: we can issue a scoped API key for the POC environment; mTLS would be preferred only if Redwood requires private deployment.

3) Security: for the trial we need logs retained for 90 days, SOC 2 attestation is sufficient, and traffic must route over our IP allowlist. We are open to Hosted with restricted egress or Dedicated depending on your guidance.

4) Owners: Tom Nguyen (Product Engineering) will drive technical integration. Procurement contact is procurement@acme-retail.com (Lia).

I’m attaching a sample export with a 48-hour representative slice (traffic_sample_202602.csv). Let us know if you need a longer window.

Sarah Li

Hi all —

Draft POC plan attached (redwood_quickstart.md). Summary here: 

Scope & timeline
- Week 0 (prep, 1–3 days): scope confirmation, API key exchange, IP allowlist, baseline metrics capture.
- Week 1 (smoke/ramp, 3 business days): ramp to 120 RPS and validate functional correctness.
- Week 2 (steady-state, 5 business days): run 120 RPS sustained windows to gather cost/latency metrics.
- Week 3 (burst tests, 2 business days): simulate promo bursts up to 450 RPS for 3–7 minute windows with monitoring and autoscale behavior.
- Week 4 (analysis & handoff, 3 business days): results, regression checks, and final recommendations.

Success metrics (concrete):
- Latency: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 250ms (measured at our edge with request sampling consistent with your traffic CSV)
- Throughput: sustained 120 RPS; handled 450 RPS bursts without >1% error-rate increase
- Cost: modeled cost-per-1M-tokens delivered and observed cost delta vs your current infra (we’ll provide an itemized estimate)
- Functional: model outputs within your acceptance sampling set (we’ll use a 500-record prompt set you provide)

Test infra & config (proposed)
- Start on Hosted: scoped API key + IP allowlist for fastest time-to-first-result. If we see egress or compliance blockers we’ll propose Dedicated for week 1 onward.
- Instance recommendation: mixed A100-style for steady-state with L4-style for burst handling (detailed instance pairs in attached doc).
- Performance knobs: enable KV prefix caching for common prompts, dynamic batching tuned to 80–120ms latency goal, and 8-bit quantization where tolerated.

Monitoring & data collection
- We will push a test dashboard link (read-only) with token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, error rates, and per-request traces tied to your request IDs.
- We’ll retain logs for 90 days per your requirement and provide an export of token usage and cost model at the end of the trial.

Ownership and points of contact
- Redwood SE (Lauren Bishop) — POC runbook, run execution, and dashboard ownership
- Redwood Pricing/Infra (Rishi Malhotra) — cost modeling and capacity sizing
- Acme Technical Owner (Tom Nguyen) — test harness, auth, and sample prompt set
- Acme Procurement (procurement@acme-retail.com) — contract and PO

Next steps (actionable)
1) Acme to confirm: 48-hour sample is representative and provide the 500-record prompt acceptance set (due Mar 6 ideally).
2) Redwood to provision scoped API key and provide test endpoints (will do once IP allowlist provided).
3) Schedule kickoff call (30 min) for Mon Mar 9 or Tue Mar 10 — suggest Mon 10:00 AM PT.

I’ve attached the quickstart + topology diagrams (redwood_quickstart.md). Ben — happy to review together with Sarah/Tom on Fri if they want a pre-kickoff sync.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
